bundle.guidance:
# Old-School Memo

An internal memorandum with the feel of a 1994 corporate print-out: black
serif on cream, ruled tables, underlined links, square corners, no shadows.
Used deliberately — for policy notices, formal internal announcements and
anything that should read as a matter of record rather than a message.

## Principles

1. **It is a document, not a page.** It should look right printed and faxed.
   Nothing may depend on hover, colour or screen width.
2. **Header block first, always.** TO, FROM, DATE, SUBJECT, in that order, in
   caps, above a hard rule. The reader must be able to file it.
3. **No ornament whatsoever.** No rounded corners, no shadows, no icons, no
   background fills except the cream page.

## Layout grid

Single column at `max-width: 40rem` — roughly a typed page — left-aligned,
with `--space-lg` between sections. Paragraph spacing, not indentation, marks
a new paragraph. Tables run the full column and are ruled on every side.
Nothing is ever centred except a table caption.

## Typography

Georgia (falling back to Times) everywhere, at `--size-body` with
`--line-body`. Headings are the same family, bold, at `--size-h1` /
`--size-h2` / `--size-h3` — barely larger than the body, distinguished by
weight and a rule. Section headings are numbered ("1.", "1.1"). Monospace is
Courier and is used only for reference numbers and code.

## Colour usage

Black (`--color-text-primary`) on cream (`--color-bg-page`). Rules and table
borders are black, never grey. Links are the dark blue `--color-brand-primary`
and are always underlined — never a colour change alone. Status colours appear
only in the rare status column of a table and always alongside the word. In
practice a correct memo is monochrome.

## Charts

Chart.js only if truly necessary, and then greyscale: bar charts using the
first three chart tokens, with hatch-free solid fills, a black axis and the
values printed above each bar. A ruled table is almost always the better
choice here.

## Diagrams

None. If a process needs a picture, write a numbered list. Mermaid is
deliberately disabled for this design system.

## Components and when to use each

- `memo-header` — the TO/FROM/DATE/SUBJECT block. Required, exactly once, at
  the very top.
- `ruled-table` — any tabular data. Fully ruled, caption above.
- `numbered-section` — a numbered heading with its body; the only heading
  form.
- `signature-block` — the closing name, title and distribution list.

## Do / don't

- **Do** write in complete sentences and the third person where it is formal.
- **Do** give the memo a reference number if your organisation uses them.
- **Don't** use emoji, exclamation marks, bold for emphasis mid-sentence, or
  any colour other than black and the link blue.
- **Don't** add a logo, a banner image or a coloured header bar.
- **Don't** use collapsible sections, tabs or anything interactive.

components.name: memo-header
components.when_to_use: Required, exactly once, at the very top of every memo.
components.html:
MEMORANDUM

TO
All staff, Data Platform
FROM
P. Simecek, Operations
DATE
15 September 2026
SUBJECT
Retention of published artifacts

components.name: ruled-table
components.description: Fully ruled table with the caption above.
components.when_to_use: All tabular data; prefer it to any chart.
components.html:
Table 1. Retention periods by artifact class
ClassPeriodAuthority
Published7 yearsPolicy 4.2
Draft90 daysPolicy 4.3

components.name: numbered-section
components.description: A numbered heading with its body text.
components.when_to_use: The only heading form in a memo. Number every section.
components.html:
2. Scope

This memorandum applies to every artifact published through the hub on or after 1 October 2026.

components.name: signature-block
components.description: Closing name, title and distribution list.
components.when_to_use: The last element of every memo.
components.html:
P. Simecek
Head of Operations

charts.notes: Greyscale bars only, values printed above each bar; a ruled table is almost always better.

diagrams.notes: Deliberately disabled: describe processes as numbered lists.
